title: Understanding the $40 per Hour Annual Salary in Australia: Tax, Super, and Take-Home Pay
description: Calculate the $40 per hour annual salary in Australia for a 38-hour week. See tax, Medicare, super, and fortnightly pay. Compare to minimum wage and average earnings.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the $40 per Hour Annual Salary in Australia

If you earn $40 per hour, you might be wondering what that translates to annually, fortnightly, and after tax. This article breaks down the $40 per hour annual salary in Australia, including tax, Medicare, and superannuation, using the standard 38-hour week.

### How to Calculate Annual Salary from Hourly Rate

The basic formula is: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, $40 per hour gives:

$40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040 per year before any deductions.

This assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a useful starting point for comparing job offers or budgeting. Our [the timesheet](/) calculator lets you enter your base rate and see the annual figure instantly.

### Fortnightly Pay

Your gross fortnightly pay would be $40 × 38 × 2 = $3,040. Many employers pay fortnightly, so this figure helps with cash flow planning. After tax and Medicare, your fortnightly take-home is approximately $2,432.

### How $40 per Hour Compares to Minimum and Average Pay

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for a full-time adult employee, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. At $40 per hour, you earn well above the minimum. If you were a casual employee, the minimum casual rate including 25% loading is $33.05 per hour – still below $40.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics' Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 shows full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, which equates to about $108,352 per year. So $79,040 is below that average. Note that this is an average, not a median for any specific job. For your occupation's pay, refer to award rates or industry guides. You can explore [pay guides](/blog) for more details.

### Tax on a $79,040 Annual Salary

For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- Over $190,000: 45%

On $79,040, your tax is calculated as:

- First $18,200: $0
- Next $26,800 (to $45,000): 15% = $4,020
- Remaining $34,040: 30% = $10,212
- Total tax: $14,232

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% on your taxable income: $1,580.80. Total deductions: $15,812.80.

Your estimated annual take-home pay is $79,040 – $15,812.80 = $63,227.20. Fortnightly, that is about $2,431.82. Remember, this is an estimate using the 2026–27 tax scale and 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds (the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here). It does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

### Superannuation (Super) Is Paid on Top

Your employer must pay super guarantee of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. For $79,040, that is $9,484.80 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost to your employer and goes into your super fund. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Casual Loading

If you are a casual employee, you may be entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. For $40 per hour, that would be $50 per hour. However, the [the timesheet](/) calculator lets you check a box to add casual loading to your base rate – never enter a rate that already includes loading. The annual figure with casual loading would be $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800 before tax.

### Award Rates and Enterprise Agreements

Many employees are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set minimum pay rates higher than the national minimum. If your $40 per hour is from an award, it may include allowances or penalty rates. Check your specific award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page provides more context on base rates.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, with optional casual loading. It also estimates tax and super. Remember that the calculator uses the assumptions described here: same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

### Summary

At $40 per hour for 38 hours a week, your annual salary is $79,040. After tax and Medicare, you take home about $63,227 per year. Super of 12% is paid on top. This is a useful estimate for budgeting, but always verify with your payslip and consult the [pay guides](/blog) for your industry.
